newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Volvo to form technical j/v with ABB.
newsitem.headline: Volvo to form technical j/v with ABB.

text.p: Swedish vehicle maker AB Volvo said on Monday it had signed an agreement with international electrical engineering company ABB to form a joint-venture in assembly line engineering and press automation.

Volvo said in a statement the new company would include Volvo Cars' businesses for assembly line engineering, press automation and lightweight welding guns in Olofstrom, Sweden and Olofstrom Automation in Canada, the U.S. and Brazil.
It said these operations had a total turnover of $106 million last year.
ABB would be the majority shareholder and bear management responsibility for the new company, it said.
"The new company will be managed by ABB Flexible Automation which employs 4,200 people in 24 countries with revenues in 1995 of $1.4 billion," Volvo said.
It said the ownership structure and the purchase price for the new company had not been fully decided.
